The candidate operations were evaluated against the actual reachability and access-control context. Internal helpers such as `setTimeRC`, `releaseTokensTo`, `giveToken`, `takeEther`, and `claimTokenBonus` are either only reachable through the constructor or through the payable fallback with `msg.sender`, or are otherwise not externally invokable with an arbitrary beneficiary. The payable fallback and its purchase/bonus paths modify only the caller’s own recorded assets or perform explicitly intended token-sale operations. - The constructor `RC(...)` is the actual constructor and is invoked only during deployment. `setTimeRC` is internal and called only by the constructor, so it is not externally reachable.

- `withdraw` and `refundEther` are protected by `onlyTokenSaleOwner`, which enforces `msg.sender == tokenSaleContract.owner()`.
- `setTime` and `changeMinimum` are also protected by `onlyTokenSaleOwner`.
- No cryptographic access-control misuse is present.
